images.title: Subtract by finding the gap
images.purpose: Show that 15 − 5 asks what must be added to 5 to reach 15, and the gap is 10.
images.composition: Two aligned horizontal bars of equal height stacked with a wide gap, a bracket showing the missing part.
images.exact_structure: One long teal #0072B2 bar made of 15 equal squares in a row. Directly under it, a bar of the same square size: 5 squares grey #6B7280 on the left, then 10 amber #E69F00 squares to the right marking the gap. Exactly 15 squares in the top bar, 5 grey and 10 amber in the lower bar.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
squares of different sizes between the two bars, or a count other than 15, 5 and 10
images.takeaway: Subtracting finds the missing number that must be added.
images.description: A row of 15 squares above a row split into 5 grey squares and 10 amber squares, showing 5 + 10 = 15 so 15 − 5 = 10.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what must be added to 5 to reach 15, then read the subtraction.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
